examples.en: A river flows along the border between the two countries.
We put up a fence on the boundary line of the land with our neighbor.
For safety, please do not cross the boundary line.
The ball went outside the boundary line.
The boundary line is drawn in red on the map.

examples.ko: 도시와 시골의 경계선이 점점 흐려지고 있어요.
examples.en: The line between city and countryside is getting blurrier.

explain: '국경'은 나라와 나라 사이에만 쓰지만, 경계선은 땅·운동장·도시처럼 어디에나 쓸 수 있어요. 눈에 보이는 선이 없어도 '선을 넘다'라고 하면 예의나 규칙을 어긴다는 뜻으로도 써요.
explain_en: '국경' (national border) is only for countries, while 경계선 fits land, sports fields, cities, anything. Even when no line is visible, '선을 넘다' (cross the line) can mean breaking manners or rules.

examples.en: I took a lump of meat out of the fridge.
First slice the big lump of meat thinly.
There are big chunks of meat in the soup.
The longer you boil a chunk of meat, the softer it gets.
Don't eat only the meat; have some vegetables too.
I bought a geun of meat in one piece at the market.

explain: 썰지 않은 큰 고기 한 덩이를 말해요. 이미 썰어 놓은 고기 조각은 '고기 조각'이나 '고기 한 점'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It means a big piece of meat that has not been sliced. Pieces that are already cut are called '고기 조각' or '고기 한 점'.

examples.en: The heel of my shoe was worn, so I left it at the shoe repair shop.

examples.ko: 구둣방 아저씨가 구두를 새것처럼 닦아 주셨어요.
examples.en: The man at the shoe repair shop polished my shoes like new.
The shoe repair shop is near the subway station.
Shoe repair shops have mostly disappeared these days.
The shoe repair shop also repairs bags.
It rained on the way to the shoe repair shop.

explain: 구두를 고치고 닦아 주는 작은 가게예요. '구두 수선집'이라고도 말해요.
explain_en: It is a small shop that repairs and shines shoes. People also call it a '구두 수선집'.

examples.en: After washing my hair, I always use conditioner.
The conditioner has run out, so I have to buy some.
I only apply conditioner to the ends of my hair.
Shall I buy conditioner too?
I make my hair soft with conditioner.

examples.ko: 샤워할 때 린스 대신 트리트먼트를 써요.
examples.en: In the shower I use a treatment instead of conditioner.

explain: 샴푸로 머리를 감은 다음에 바르는 제품이에요. 한국에서 '린스'와 '컨디셔너'는 보통 같은 제품으로 봐요. '린스를 바르다', '린스를 헹구다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It is the product you apply after washing hair with shampoo. In Korea '린스' and '컨디셔너' are usually treated as the same product. Say '린스를 바르다' to apply it.

en: gaps; the spaces here and there between things

examples.en: I tucked sticky notes in between the pages of the book.
I stretch for a moment in between bouts of work.
Sunlight comes in through the gaps between the trees.
The wind feels cool when I walk between the buildings.
I put a comma between every pair of sentences.

examples.ko: 연습 사이사이의 짧은 휴식이 도움이 돼요.
examples.en: The short breaks between practice sessions help.

explain: '사이'는 하나의 틈이고, '사이사이'는 여러 군데의 틈을 함께 말해요. 그래서 '나무 사이'는 두 나무의 중간이고, '나무 사이사이'는 나무들 곳곳의 빈 곳이에요. 시간에도 써서 일과 일 사이의 짧은 시간들을 가리켜요.
explain_en: 사이 is one gap, while 사이사이 refers to many gaps at once. 나무 사이 is the space between two trees, but 나무 사이사이 is the open spaces here and there among the trees. It also works for time, meaning the short moments between tasks.

examples.en: I clipped and saved a newspaper article.
I save good articles and read them later.
I keep my articles in a clipping folder.

examples.ko: 이 게시물을 스크랩하면 내 보관함에 저장돼요.
examples.en: If you save this post, it is stored in my archive.

examples.ko: 스크랩한 글이 너무 많아서 정리해야 해요.
examples.en: I have too many saved articles and need to organize them.

examples.ko: 인터넷 기사 스크랩은 숙제에 도움이 됐어요.
examples.en: Saving internet articles helped with my homework.

explain: 신문이나 잡지에서 필요한 기사를 오려 모으는 일이에요. 요즘은 인터넷 글을 저장하는 일도 '스크랩'이라고 하고, 동사는 '스크랩하다'예요.
explain_en: It means cutting out articles from newspapers or magazines and keeping them. Today it also means saving online posts, and the verb is '스크랩하다'.

examples.en: I season meat with soy sauce.
My mother seasoned the fish deliciously.
I will season the chicken this evening.
I boil water while seasoning.
Season the vegetables and mix them well.
It was marinated for a long time, so the flavor is deep.

explain: '양념'은 명사로도 많이 써요. '양념치킨', '양념장'처럼 다른 말 앞뒤에 붙기도 해요. 간을 해서 고기를 미리 재워 두는 일은 '재우다'라고도 해요.
explain_en: '양념' is very often used as a noun, and attaches to other words as in '양념치킨' and '양념장'. Leaving seasoned meat to sit beforehand is also called '재우다'.

examples.en: I drizzle plenty of olive oil on my salad.
I coated the pan with olive oil and stir-fried the vegetables.
I bought a bottle of olive oil at the supermarket.
These days they say olive oil is good for your health.
I dip bread in olive oil.
We ran out of olive oil, so I used cooking oil.

explain: '올리브오일'이라고도 많이 불러요. 한국 음식에는 참기름, 들기름, 식용유를 주로 쓰고, 올리브유는 샐러드나 파스타 같은 서양 요리에 써요. 팬에는 '두르다', 샐러드에는 '뿌리다'를 써요.
explain_en: People often call it 'olive oil' (올리브오일) too. Korean cooking mostly uses sesame oil, perilla oil and cooking oil, while olive oil goes into salads and pasta. For a pan you say '두르다' (coat), and for a salad you say '뿌리다' (drizzle).

examples.en: The company deposits my salary into my account every month.
I transferred the meal money to my friend yesterday.

examples.ko: 내일까지 이 계좌로 십만 원을 입금할 거예요.
examples.en: I will deposit 100,000 won into this account by tomorrow.
Be sure to check the name of the person depositing.

examples.ko: 아직 입금하지 않아서 주문이 안 됐어요.
examples.en: The order did not go through because I have not paid yet.
Please send a text message after you deposit the money.

explain: 돈을 넣는 것은 '입금하다', 빼는 것은 '출금하다'예요. '송금하다'는 돈을 보내는 행동에, '입금하다'는 계좌에 돈을 넣는 행동에 초점이 있어요.
explain_en: Putting money in is 'ipgeumhada' and taking it out is '출금하다'. '송금하다' focuses on sending money, while 'ipgeumhada' focuses on money going into an account.

examples.en: I bought two tickets at the ticket office.
I lost my ticket, so I bought another.
Please show your ticket to the driver.
How much is one ticket?
You have to buy holiday tickets early.
I booked the ticket in advance.

explain: 버스나 기차 같은 탈것의 표를 넓게 말해요. 어떤 차인지 분명히 할 때는 '버스표', '기차표'라고 해요.
explain_en: It broadly means a ticket for a bus, train or similar vehicle. When you want to be specific, say '버스표' or '기차표'.

examples.ko: 겨울에는 털모자를 쓰면 귀가 안 시려요.
examples.en: If you wear a woolen hat in winter, your ears won't get cold.

examples.ko: 이건 할머니가 손수 짜 주신 털모자예요.
examples.en: This is a woolen hat my grandmother knitted by hand for me.
The woolen hat is big, so it keeps slipping down.
It's snowing, so wear a woolen hat when you go out.

examples.ko: 털모자는 세탁기에 돌리면 줄어들 수 있어요.
examples.en: A woolen hat can shrink if you put it in the washing machine.
The red woolen hat has a pom-pom on it.

explain: 모자는 '쓰다'를 쓰니까 '털모자를 쓰다'라고 해요. 털실로 짠 모자는 '니트 모자'나 '비니'라고도 해요. 짝으로 '털장갑', '목도리'가 같이 나와요.
explain_en: Hats take the verb '쓰다', so you say '털모자를 쓰다'. A hat knitted from wool yarn may also be called a '니트 모자' or '비니'. It is often paired with '털장갑' and '목도리' (scarf).
